rationale:
`assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md` has front matter, so it is a bundled skill and a site of `requirements.cli.skill_conventions`.

The front matter `description` says when to use the skill in terms of the user's task:
- It applies during design sessions and before changing code, tests, or requirement text in a Habeas-tracked project.
- It applies even when the user only asks for a feature, bug fix, CLI flag, test, dependency bump, or wording tweak.
- It also applies when writing or revising reference chapters.

The description names other bundled skills only to redirect: "Not for moving code or requirements… use habeas-refactor. For validation findings, use habeas-evidence." The requirement permits this (MAY), and it fits the case where an agent could confuse the skills.

No violation matches were listed, and I found no gap.

text: Each bundled skill's description MUST state when to use it in terms of the user's task. It MAY name another bundled skill to use instead where an agent could confuse the two. Each bundled skill, recognized by its front matter, is a site:
